title: Office move steering committee
lines: Good afternoon, everyone. This is the steering committee for the office move, and we have six items today. Let's start with the timeline.
The landlord has confirmed we can get the keys on the first of February. The fit-out will take about eight weeks after that.
So we'd move in at the start of April?
Early April, yes, assuming the council approves the plans for the kitchen and the bathrooms.
When do we expect the council decision?
They said four to six weeks. We submitted the plans last Monday.
Okay. Olivia, what does that mean for the lease on the current office?
Our current lease ends on the thirty first of March. We can extend month to month, but the rent goes up by twenty percent.
Twenty percent is steep. Is that negotiable?
I've asked. They'll come back to me next week. Worst case, one extra month costs us about nine thousand dollars.
Let's plan for one extra month as a contingency, and hope we don't need it.
Can I raise the network setup? That's the thing most likely to delay us.
The building has fibre, but the provider needs ten weeks' notice to connect us. If we order it after the keys, we'll miss April.
Can we order it before we have the keys?
Yes, if the landlord signs the access form. I sent it to them on Tuesday, but I haven't heard back.
I'll chase the landlord tomorrow. I'm meeting their property manager anyway.
Thanks, Frank. If we get the form signed this week, we're fine.
Good. Next item, furniture. Thandi, you were collecting quotes.
I have three quotes. The cheapest is forty two thousand, and the one I'd recommend is fifty one thousand, because it includes installation.
The desks are the same. The recommended one has better chairs and a five year warranty, instead of two years.
Then I think the extra cost is worth it, especially with the installation included.
I agree. Installation alone would cost us five or six thousand otherwise.
Any objections to going with the fifty one thousand dollar quote?
Then that's decided. Thandi, please accept that quote and ask for delivery in the last week of March.
Will do. I'll send the purchase order to finance by Wednesday.
Next, the seating plan. James, you were going to survey the teams.
Yes. About seventy percent of people want to keep fixed desks, and thirty percent are happy to hot desk.
The sales team wants to sit near the meeting rooms, and the engineers want the quiet corner away from the kitchen.
That seems reasonable. Can you draft a seating plan for the next meeting?
I can have a first draft by the twentieth of January.
Great. Olivia, the budget. Where do we stand overall?
The approved budget is three hundred and twenty thousand. With the furniture decision, we've committed two hundred and ninety.
That leaves thirty thousand for contingencies, which is a bit thin given the lease risk.
The fit-out quote also has a ten percent allowance for surprises, so we have some cushion there.
Okay. Let's keep an eye on it, and report back if the contingency drops below twenty thousand.
One open question from my side. Are we keeping the old furniture, or selling it?
Good question. I don't think we've decided.
Some of it could go to the Sydney office. They asked for desks last year.
Let's find out what Sydney actually needs before we decide. Can someone ask them?
I'll ask the Sydney office manager this week.
Thank you. Last item, communication to staff. I'd like to send an update before Christmas.
I can write the first draft, and include the seating survey results.
Perfect. Let me summarise the actions. Frank chases the landlord about the fibre access form tomorrow.
Thandi accepts the furniture quote, sends the purchase order by Wednesday, and asks Sydney about the old furniture.
James drafts the seating plan by the twentieth of January and writes the staff update. Olivia follows up on the lease extension next week.
And Raj orders the fibre as soon as the form is signed.
Great. Thanks everyone. We'll meet again in two weeks.
